items.question: Q4 (pre-registered): sparse parity, how does the onset of the planted interaction scale with n, per order k? Fit log(median onset over seeds) on log n for each k and lr with a bootstrap over seeds; reference n^(k-1) (exponents 1, 2, 3); v0 hint about 1.0 (k=2) and 1.2-1.6 (k=3).
items.definition_used: Literal (registered): onset = step of the planted subset's first ri_events activation (kind == 'activation'); the event step is the first active checkpoint steps[t0] (events.py), so the onset lies in (step_lo, step]. Amended (Amendment 1 C, decides): the first activation or reactivation event that is not left-censored (t0 > 0) and at whose checkpoint t0 the planted subset's Walsh coefficient has the sign of its value at the last checkpoint. Median over all seeds of the current sky (coarse + refinement) at each (k, lr, n): k=2 lr=0.03: seeds per n [10, 10, 10, 10, 10] (50 runs); k=2 lr=0.1: seeds per n [10, 10, 10, 10, 10] (50 runs); k=3 lr=0.03: seeds per n [12, 12, 12, 12, 12] (60 runs); k=3 lr=0.1: seeds per n [12, 12, 12, 12, 12] (60 runs); k=4 lr=0.03: seeds per n [12, 12, 10] (34 runs); k=4 lr=0.1: seeds per n [12, 12, 10] (34 runs). OLS of ln(median) on ln(n) over n = 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 (k=4: 16, 24, 32). 95 % percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20261112, seeds resampled with replacement within each n, medians recomputed and refit; the same resample indices for every measure within (k, lr), so slope differences are paired. Runs without an onset are set to the step budget (20k/60k/150k). Ambiguities and alternatives: (a) 'activation event' read as activation or reactivation (alternative: kind == 'activation' only); (b) sign checked at t0 (alternatives: at both confirming checkpoints t0 and t0+1; a sign-aware recomputation from the curve, q <= 0.01, ri >= min_effect and final sign at two consecutive checkpoints, t0 > 0). Every alternative gives the same onset in 288 of 288 runs.
items.amended_result: Identical to the literal result: Amendment C changes no parity onset (0 of 288 runs differ). Every planted subset has exactly one event (an activation; no extinction or reactivation), none at the first checkpoint (RI = 0 and q > 0.01 at step 0 in all runs; max |f| at step 0 = 0.0142), and the coefficient at the activation checkpoint has the final (negative) sign in every run. Slopes: k=2 lr=0.03: 1.88 [1.70, 1.92]; k=2 lr=0.1: 1.75 [1.62, 1.88]; k=3 lr=0.03: 1.92 [1.68, 2.10]; k=3 lr=0.1: 1.80 [1.54, 1.93]; k=4 lr=0.03: 2.18 [1.91, 2.41]; k=4 lr=0.1: 2.18 [1.91, 2.38]. Reference: k=2 lr=0.03: reference 1 outside CI; k=2 lr=0.1: reference 1 outside CI; k=3 lr=0.03: reference 2 inside CI; k=3 lr=0.1: reference 2 outside CI; k=4 lr=0.03: reference 3 outside CI; k=4 lr=0.1: reference 3 outside CI.
items.interpretation: The planted-interaction onset grows as a power of n with exponent 1.75-1.88 for k=2, 1.80-1.92 for k=3 and 2.18 for k=4 (3 points). The exponent rises only weakly with k, far less than the n^(k-1) reference: for k=2 it is well above 1 (CIs exclude 1), for k=3 the CI includes 2 at lr 0.03 (1.92 [1.68, 2.10]) but not at lr 0.1 (1.80 [1.54, 1.93]), and for k=4 it is well below 3 (2.18 [1.91, 2.38]). The exponent barely depends on the learning rate for k=3 and k=4; lr 0.03 onsets are 3.0-4.0 times the lr 0.1 onsets (lr ratio 3.3). Against the v0 hint, the RI onset exponent on the v0 range (n=16-32, lr 0.1) is about 2 for both k=2 and k=3, larger than the v0 numbers, which were exponents of the steps to 90 % test accuracy (see q4_photometric: that measure reproduces v0). Measures compatible with the reference (CI contains k-1): iv_t_test_acc90 k=2 lr=0.1 (0.94 [0.87, 1.05]); ii_amended k=3 lr=0.03 (1.92 [1.68, 2.10]); iii_fourier_gated k=3 lr=0.03 (1.92 [1.68, 2.10]). The onset is a low-threshold crossing (detection threshold |f| 0.062-0.081; median |f| at the onset checkpoint k=2: 0.071, k=3: 0.236, k=4: 0.160), and its exponent depends on the threshold (q4_fit_strength): for k=2 the exponent falls from 1.71-1.75 at |f| >= 0.0447 to 0.35-0.36 at |f| >= 0.9, so 'the' exponent of parity learning is not a single number here.
items.caveats: Three- and five-point log-log fits over a factor of 4 (k=4: factor 2) in n are weak evidence of a power law; for k=2 the local slope falls significantly from n=16-32 to n=32-64 (see q4_fit_strength). Onsets are quantised to the 60-point log grid: above step 10, consecutive checkpoints differ by a factor 1.09-1.37, i.e. 0.09-0.32 in ln, comparable to the fit residuals; the percentile bootstrap of grid-valued medians is lumpy and can be asymmetric around the point estimate (e.g. k=2 lr 0.03: 1.88 [1.70, 1.92]). Using step_lo instead of the event step lowers slopes by up to 0.23 (k=4 lr=0.03); a bracket-jittered bootstrap is reported in q4_fit_strength. For k=2, holding the detection threshold fixed in n gives exponents 1.69-1.70 (lr 0.03) and 1.54-1.60 (lr 0.1), 0.18 and 0.15 below the RI exponent. So part of the k=2 exponent comes from a detection rule that changes with n: the number of scanned candidates grows from m = 136 at n=16 to 2080 at n=64. Checks: planted subset found once in 288 of 288 curves; ri_events rows of the planted subset equal detect_events(curve, alpha=0.01) in 288 of 288; objects.t_test_acc90 equals the light-curve recomputation in 288 of 288; final Walsh coefficient negative in 288 of 288 (range -0.99996 to -0.99883; learned parity = -1 convention); minimum final test accuracy 1.

items.question: Q4 with the Fourier baseline: does the onset exponent from the Walsh coefficient of the planted inputs agree with the RI exponent (it should, with uniform probes)? Amendment 1 A defines the gated Fourier onset.
items.definition_used: Registered Fourier onset (literal, check-2 definition): first checkpoint with |f| >= eps, eps = 0.0447 solving ln 2 - h((1+eps)/2) = min_effect = 0.001 (no persistence). Amended (A, decides): first of two consecutive checkpoints where R = ln 2 - h((1+|f|)/2) satisfies R - 1/(2N) >= min_effect and min(1, m chi2_1.sf(2NR)) <= alpha = 0.01, with m = meta n_candidates (136 to 43,744 depending on k and n) and N = meta min_effect_n = 4096; f = the stored Walsh coefficient of the planted inputs. The gate equals |f| >= k2_n16: 0.0619, k2_n24: 0.0648, k2_n32: 0.0668, k2_n48: 0.0695, k2_n64: 0.0714, k3_n16: 0.0678, k3_n24: 0.0718, k3_n32: 0.0745, k3_n48: 0.0783, k3_n64: 0.0808, k4_n16: 0.0720, k4_n24: 0.0772, k4_n32: 0.0806. Same fit and paired bootstrap as q4. Alternative: the gate plus Amendment C (t0 > 0 and final sign) changes the onset in 0 of 288 runs; the gate fires at the first checkpoint in 0 runs.
items.interpretation: For k=3 and k=4 the RI and gated-Fourier onsets have identical medians in every (lr, n) cell, so the exponents are identical. For k=2 the RI exponent is larger by 0.04 (lr 0.03) and 0.17 (lr 0.1); the paired CI excludes 0 at lr 0.1 (0.038 to 0.262). The cause is that the RI event fires 1-3 checkpoints before the gate in 22 of 100 k=2 runs (21 of them at n <= 32; by n: {16: 8, 24: 7, 32: 6, 64: 1}): the gate uses m * p, a conservative stand-in for the BH q-value, and the stored q is smaller when other subsets are also significant. At the RI onset checkpoint of the 30 runs (all k) where RI fires first, the median stored q is 0.0051 against a median stand-in of 0.0343; the stand-in is above alpha in 30 of them. Over all runs, q < stand-in at the RI onset in 185 of 288. With a gradually growing coefficient, a one-checkpoint shift at small n moves the slope. So RI and Fourier carry the same information here, as expected with uniform probes. The remaining k=2 difference comes from the gate's definition, not from the instrument. The bare Fourier onset (registered check-2 threshold) precedes the gated one by 0-5 checkpoints for k=2, as Amendment A anticipated, and by 0-1 for k=3 and k=4 (distribution in key_numbers).
items.caveats: The gate approximates the BH q-value of the planted subset by m * p (Bonferroni). The stored q-values come from the full scan, so the RI event can pass before the stand-in does. Exponents of threshold crossings depend on the threshold level (q4_fit_strength).

items.question: Q4 photometric reference: how does t_test_acc90 (first light-curve step with test accuracy >= 0.9) scale with n, and does it reproduce the v0 hint?
items.definition_used: t_test_acc90 from objects.parquet (equal to the recomputation from the light curves in every run); never reached = censored at the budget (0 runs). Same fit and bootstrap as q4. v0 baseline recomputed from DR0 with scripts/analyze_dr0.py's rule: parity-wide, online data, learned runs (final test acc >= 0.9; at these settings all were learned), median t_test_acc90 at n = 16, 24, 32, pooled over widths (the published hint) and width 512 only (the v1 width), same bootstrap.
items.interpretation: v1 reproduces v0 on the same configuration: at width 512, lr 0.1, n = 16-32 the t_test_acc90 medians and exponents agree (k=2 lr=0.1: medians [63, 103, 151] slope 1.26 [1.10, 1.47]; k=3 lr=0.1: medians [606, 1057, 1845] slope 1.59 [1.40, 1.77]; v0 width 512 in key_numbers). The v0 hint was an exponent of steps to 90 % test accuracy pooled over widths; recomputed from DR0 (lr 0.1) it is 1.03 for k=2 and 1.53 for k=3. Over the wider v1 range, t_test_acc90 grows as n^0.94-1.23 for k=2 (concave: local slope 0.63-0.74 from n=32 to 64), n^1.52-1.80 for k=3 and n^1.75-1.83 for k=4. For k=3 and k=4 every t_test_acc90 CI excludes the n^(k-1) reference: k=3 lr=0.03 1.80 [1.68, 1.92]; k=3 lr=0.1 1.52 [1.43, 1.64]; k=4 lr=0.03 1.75 [1.65, 2.06]; k=4 lr=0.1 1.83 [1.63, 2.06]. The RI onset exponent is larger than the t_test_acc90 exponent in every (k, lr); the paired CIs exclude 0 except: k=3 lr=0.03. So the RI lead over accuracy shrinks in relative terms as n grows (q4_lead).
items.caveats: t_test_acc90 lives on the light-curve grid (parity-k2: 71 points, parity-k3: 73 points, parity-k4: 74 points), which is finer than the 60-point RI grid and contains it; a run's t_test_acc90 can therefore fall between two RI checkpoints. The v0 baseline used a [30000] step budget and its own evaluation grid, so the v0 comparison is approximate.

items.question: Q4: how does the RI onset relate to t_test_acc90 (lead in steps, as a ratio, in checkpoints)?
items.definition_used: Per run: lead = t_test_acc90 - amended onset (ii) in steps; ratio = onset (ii) / t_test_acc90; lead in RI checkpoints = index of the first RI checkpoint with test accuracy >= 0.9 (the RI grid is a subset of the light-curve grid, so test accuracy is known there) minus the index of the onset checkpoint. Medians and IQR per (k, lr, n) and pooled over n.

items.interpretation: The RI onset comes after the 90 % accuracy crossing on the common RI grid in 0 of 288 runs. For k=2 it leads clearly: 100 of 100 runs, by 2-15 RI checkpoints, with median test accuracy 0.63 at the onset. The ratio onset/t_test_acc90 rises with n (lr 0.1: 0.20 at n=16 to 0.61 at n=64; lr 0.03: 0.32 to 0.69), because the onset exponent exceeds the accuracy exponent. For k=3 and k=4 the coefficient jumps: from |f| >= 0.0808 to |f| >= 0.5 takes a median of k=2: 5, k=3: 1, k=4: 1 RI checkpoints. The onset is then typically one RI checkpoint ahead (pooled median ratio 0.86-0.87, about one grid step) or on the same checkpoint (k=3: 42 of 120; k=4: 6 of 68). So the lead for k >= 3 is at the grid resolution. As noted in v0, this is a low threshold on the same Walsh coefficient being crossed before a high one, not evidence that RI sees more than accuracy.
items.caveats: In steps, 4 k=3 and 0 k=4 runs show a negative lead, because t_test_acc90 falls on a light-curve step between two RI checkpoints; on the RI grid these are the same checkpoint. Ratios for k >= 3 take few discrete values set by the grid spacing.

items.question: Q4: how strong is the evidence for a power law, and how robust is the exponent?
items.definition_used: (1) Residuals of the ln-ln OLS fit. (2) Sub-range slopes from the same bootstrap: n = 16-32 vs 32-64 for k=2,3 and 16-24 vs 24-32 for k=4, with a paired CI of their difference. (3) Bracket-jittered bootstrap: each resampled onset is drawn log-uniformly within its bracket (step_lo, step], so the CI includes the checkpoint quantisation; same for t_test_acc90 with its light-curve bracket. (4) Onset at step_lo or the geometric bracket midpoint. (5) Threshold sweep (supplementary, not a criterion): the first of two consecutive checkpoints t0 > 0 with sign-corrected f >= c for fixed c, and the Amendment-A gate threshold held fixed at the region's smallest / largest m (this removes the gate's n-dependence).

items.interpretation: The five-point fits have R2 >= 0.990, but residuals reach 0.177 in ln units, about one checkpoint gap. For k=2 a single power law does not hold: the local slope falls from 1.96-2.17 (n=16-32) to 1.46-1.62 (n=32-64), with difference CIs excluding 0 at both learning rates, also under bracket jitter. For k=3 the sub-range slopes are compatible (difference CIs include 0), but each sub-range CI is 0.67-1.04 wide. The k=4 three-point fit (R2 = 1.000 with 1 degree of freedom) is no evidence of a power law: its sub-range CIs span 1.40-3.15. The exponent also depends on which threshold defines 'onset'. For k=2 it falls from 1.71-1.75 at |f| >= 0.0447 to 0.35-0.36 at |f| >= 0.9; for k=3 from 1.86-2.00 to 1.24-1.53; for k=4 from 2.18-2.29 to 1.32. Holding the gate threshold fixed in n gives k=2 exponents 1.69-1.70 (lr 0.03) and 1.54-1.60 (lr 0.1), 0.15-0.18 below the RI onset exponent. For k=3 and k=4 the fixed-gate exponents differ from the RI exponent by at most 0.03. The robust statements are three. Low-threshold onset exponents (RI, gated and bare Fourier, fixed |f| 0.0447 and 0.0808, fixed gates) lie between 1.54 and 2.29 across all k and lr, rising only weakly with k. No measure approaches 3 for k=4. The measures whose CI contains k-1 are listed in q4. A three- or five-point fit over a factor 2-4 in n cannot distinguish a power law from a curved relation.
items.caveats: The sub-range and sweep analyses are added robustness checks, not pre-registered criteria. Bootstrap CIs of grid-valued medians are lumpy; the jittered CIs are the more honest ones.

description: Sky v1 pre-registered question 4 (sparse parity: onset scaling with n per order k), with Amendment 1 items A and C. Generated by scripts/analysis_v1/parity_scaling.py.

settings.unit: seeds resampled within each n, paired across measures within (k, lr)
settings.median: numpy (mean of the two middle values for even seed counts)
settings.onset_step: event step = first active checkpoint (events.py step = steps[t0])
settings.censoring: no onset within budget -> budget value
